## Grids - 0.01 Longitude x 0.01 Latitude

```{r Construct a 0.01 x 0.01 decimal degree grid}
#| code-summary: "Construct & Plot 0.01 x 0.01 decimal degree grid"
#| code-line-numbers: "|1-3|5-7|8-9|10|12-15"

# Filter to Manhattan County
manhattan_county <- census_county %>%
  filter(STATEFP == "36" & COUNTYFP == "061")

# Create the grid & trim it to Manhattan
# cellsize is in the units of the CRS (decimal degrees)
manhattan_grid_decimal_01 <- manhattan_county %>%
  st_make_grid(cellsize = c(0.01, 0.01), square = TRUE) %>%
  st_sf() %>%
  st_intersection(manhattan_county)

# Plot
leaflet(manhattan_grid_decimal_01) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addPolygons(weight = 0.5, opacity = 1.0)
```

::: {.notes}
- Go by decimal degrees
- Nice because you can just truncate your coordinates to a certain number of decimals
- Gets narrower as you move toward the North and South poles
- Manhattan's grid is angled 29 degrees
:::
